data.name: Muawiyah
data.gender_notes: Muawiyah is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muawiyah is derived from the Arabic root 'waa-waw-yaa' which conveys the idea of being harmonious or causing harmony. It is a name associated with a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The name Muawiyah carries the meaning “One who causes harmony” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Muawiyah usually hope their child will grow to embody one who causes harmony and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan was a notable companion of the Prophet and a significant figure in Islamic history, known for his diplomatic and leadership skills.
data.etymology: Muawiyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who causes harmony.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muawiyah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: معاوية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم معاوية مشتق من الجذر العربي معى وياء، ويعني المرجو أو المحب، وقد كان هذا الاسم شائعا في العهد النبوي، ويعتبر معاوية بن أبي سفيان أحد أهم الشخصيات في التاريخ الإسلامي

in_urdu.name: معاویہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: معاویہ کا نام عربی gốc معى سے ماخوذ ہے، جو مرجو یا محبوب کے معنی میں ہے، اور یہ نام برصغیر پاک و ہند میں بھی مسلمانوں کے درمیان شائع ہوا ہے

in_hindi.name: मुआविया
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुआविया नाम अरबी मूल معى से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ प्रिय या अभीष्ट होता है, और यह नाम भारतीय मुसलमानों के बीच भी प्रसिद्ध हुआ है

in_pashto.name: معاویه

data.cultural_impact: Muawiyah is most notably associated with Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, the first Umayyad Caliph, who ruled the Islamic empire from 661 to 680 AD. He consolidated the Umayyad amirate in Damascus into a powerful and influential dynasty that ruled the caliphate for over 200 years. Muawiyah is also known for his diplomatic abilities, military leadership, and his efforts in spreading Islam to new lands. Today, Muawiyah is remembered as a significant figure in Islamic history and a symbol of political stability and unity during a turbulent period in early Islamic history.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Muawiyah signifies the idea of creating harmony and peace in the quality of one's character and actions. It encourages the ability to bring others together and to find common ground, even in the midst of differing viewpoints or ideologies. The name serves as a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's message of unity, compassion, and patience, and the importance of striving for peace and harmony, both within oneself and in the wider world.

historical_references.reference: Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (570-642 CE) was the fifth caliph of the Islamic Ummah and the founder of the Umayyad Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Muawiyah ruled the Islamic empire from Damascus after the death of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and is considered the first non-Quraysh ruler of the Islamic state.
